title: Chapter 240: Real Stories
html:
“No. 4, before you begin, I must warn you.” The first man on the right turned toward Chen Ge. “Your story must be true. We have our own means of detecting falsehoods. If you fabricate anything, you will be punished accordingly.”

“I know the rules.”

“Then begin.”

Chen Ge considered his options, then began his first tale. “This is a true story about a friend of mine. His surname was Wang. He loved his wife deeply, but several months ago, she vanished without a trace.

“He reported her disappearance and searched the entire city, posting missing-person notices everywhere he went. People pitied him. The investigating officers saw how completely he had doted on his wife and understood his desperation.

“But true fairy tales do not exist. After six months, his wife remained missing. The police had given up, but he refused. Finding her became his sole reason to live. Every morning, he left home early with a stack of notices and returned only late at night.

“He repeated the routine day after day until, at last, his efforts seemed to bear fruit. A message arrived from his wife.

“Save me…

“It came from her phone. The message was brief, but it filled his heart with boundless terror.

“He had concealed a secret from everyone: he was responsible for his wife’s disappearance. He had murdered her and hidden the body. His endless search was self-punishment, a way to exhaust himself and ease his guilt. He had never expected his dead wife to contact him from beyond the grave.

“He hastily removed her body from a hidden compartment in the house, drove into the countryside, and buried it. He believed that would end the matter. Instead, stranger things began.

“Whenever he awoke, pieces of his wife’s clothing lay on the bed beside him, as though she had returned during the night.

“But how could the person he buried return in the night?

“He gathered his tools and returned to the countryside, moving the body deeper into the forest. Yet no matter what he did, he awoke to find her belongings around him. It was as though she climbed from the grave each night and returned the moment he fell asleep.

“His fear mounted. Messages from his wife continued appearing on his phone, though he never remembered receiving them. The only explanation was that they arrived while he slept.

“Then matters worsened. Sometimes, he awoke wearing the clothes in which his wife had died. Near collapse, he knew the problem lay with her corpse. He returned to the grave to move her one final time.

“To prevent her return, he devised a mad solution: he would seal her body inside the wall of an old apartment building.

“As his wife disappeared into the wall, he sighed with relief. This time, she could never come back.” Chen Ge stopped abruptly. “That is the end.”

“That’s it?” The two at the table were deep in the story. “Then what happened next? What happened to your friend?”

Chen Ge had recounted Wang Qi’s story. He wanted to add, That ‘friend’ met me and is now rotting in prison.

“Your story isn’t finished, right?” the first man on the left said with annoyance.

“That is all I know. Anything more would be a lie.” Chen Ge made his voice sound older. The first man on the left exchanged glances with the others, and everyone turned toward the fifth figure on that side. A black robe concealed the person entirely, leaving not an inch of skin exposed.

Feeling their attention, the figure spoke. “I cannot read him clearly, but the story appears to be true.”

“A decent tale, but I dislike how it makes me feel.” The first man on the left placed his left hand on the table—apparently casting a vote. Eight of the remaining nine did the same. Only the man interested in Chen Ge’s mask abstained.

“Nine votes in favor and one abstention. It seems tonight’s main course has been chosen.” The man on the left chuckled darkly. The others regarded Chen Ge with open malice.

Chen Ge tried calling Zhang Ya, but there was no response. He knew that if he did not do something, he was going to be in grave danger.

“Don’t be hasty. That was only my first story.” Chen Ge remained perfectly calm, the mask’s lips twisted into a smile. “As I said, I have many.”

Initially, the other new members had sighed in relief, but they got tense again.

“Many stories?” The man interested in his mask studied him. “The Ghost Stories Society’s rules state that anyone who tells three verified true ghost stories may make a request or choose to leave. If you can provide two more, our opinion of you may change.”

His statement was approved by the rest. Only the first man on the right hesitated. “No. 10, you seem to value this new member a lot.”

“I just feel he is very interesting.”

The black-robed figures around the table each had a number. They never used names, not even aliases.

“True ghost stories are not so easily found. An ordinary person would break after encountering even one or two.” The man on the left withdrew his hand from the table. “Let us hope he is not foolish enough to lie.”

Chen Ge did not interrupt their exchanges. After all, he was trying to drag out the time.

“Tell us the rest of your stories.”

“My second story is another real story that happened to my friend.”

Chen Ge first described Fan Yu watching his parents fall into the well, then living in a ghost-filled house with his murderous aunt. Next came the Pen Spirit and the girl suffering from depression. When Zhang Ya still did not awaken, he continued with Men Nan washing his hair at midnight and the monster steadily invading his dreams.

Finally, he adopted Xu Yin’s perspective and told the young man’s bloody love story.

Every account was true. By the time he finished, the society’s members had fallen silent. What kind of life had this man lived?

His ‘friends’ were invariably sick or mad, and every few years, one of them died. Yet this fellow remained alive and had come here to tell their stories. Could he be the true culprit behind them all?
